title: Publish scheduler usage-measurement consumer surface
description: Objective: make the landed provider-neutral usage measurement contract executable through the bare @moe/scheduler package root so a provider telemetry composer can use the production authority rather than copy its source/coverage matrix. Deliverable: a curated root export of UsageMeasurementRecord, normalizeUsageMeasurement, the exact coverage/source/code/layer vocabularies and required type closure, with package-root/runtime tests. Consumer: task-159f4c21ef9149e8a65f24735c9c1475. NOT in scope: new normalization semantics, provider parsing, pricing, benchmark gates, or edits to the 250-line measurement kernels. Owned paths: packages/scheduler/src/index.ts and packages/scheduler/src/index-surface.test.ts only. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test.
definitionOfDone: @moe/scheduler root exports normalizeUsageMeasurement plus UsageMeasurementRecord, NormalizedMeasurement, PricebookBinding, coverage/source/code/layer vocabularies, and the exact callable type closure; no direct enumerator, policy, fixture, or incidental helper leaks.

Package-root exact namespace tests and a plain-Node bare-specifier probe prove every new runtime binding loads and invokes the production normalizer; generated runtime names have exact non-zero cardinality.

Root-driven tests pin UNKNOWN/null, PARTIAL/lower-bound, source/coverage, truncated-completion, and malformed-record semantics with their existing exact CONTRACT or MEASUREMENT code/layer; production kernel behavior remains byte-for-byte unchanged.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test exits 0.
taskRails: Do not edit packages/scheduler/src/budget/budget-contract.ts or budget-measurement.ts; both are focused 250-line landed authorities.
Publish the existing normalizer and closed vocabularies; do not clone SOURCE_COVERAGES or introduce provider-specific rules.
Tests assert exact stable reason code and refusing layer and generated case counts are non-zero.
Consumer task is task-159f4c21ef9149e8a65f24735c9c1475; root loadability alone is not the final provider composition.

implementationPlan.description: RE-MEASURE, DO NOT WRITE. This board's rail makes description claims stale by default and this one claims a gap is OPEN, so confirm it is still open rather than already closed by a peer: (a) `grep -n "normalizeUsageMeasurement\|MEASUREMENT_ISSUE_CODES\|BUDGET_MEASUREMENT_COVERAGES" packages/scheduler/src/index.ts` must return ZERO hits — if it returns any, STOP and report_blocked rather than land a duplicate publication; (b) `grep -c ''` on budget-contract.ts and budget-measurement.ts must both still read 250, confirming the two kernels this task may not edit; (c) re-read the exact expected code/layer pairs in budget-measurement.test.ts for the malformed-envelope, UNKNOWN/null, source-coverage-mismatch, truncated-completion and pricebook-binding cases and copy them into the step note — step 4 must mirror those exact pairs, never re-derive them; (d) confirm index-surface.test.ts:130 still compares `Object.keys(scheduler).sort()` against an UNSORTED `EXPECTED_EXPORTS.map(...)`, which is what forces sorted insertion; (e) record the current pinned count at :126. Record all five results in the step note.

TDD RED on the namespace contract. In index-surface.test.ts insert the seven new runtime values into EXPECTED_EXPORTS at their ASCII-sorted positions — BUDGET_ISSUE_CODES, BUDGET_MEASUREMENT_COVERAGES and BUDGET_MEASUREMENT_SOURCES before BUDGET_RESERVATION_ISSUE_CODES; MEASUREMENT_ISSUE_CODES and MEASUREMENT_ISSUE_LAYERS between MAX_GRAPH_KEY_CODE_UNITS and MIN_GATED_DESCENDANTS_FOR_REVIEW; SUPPORTED_SOURCE_PARSER_VERSIONS after SUPERSESSION_REFUSAL_CODES; normalizeUsageMeasurement between isFairnessIdentity and parseClock — each tagged "array" except the normalizer, which is "function". Bump the hand-written count at :126 accordingly and add a clause to the doc comment above the table naming this group, so the transcription rationale does not detach from the table. Add a NEGATIVE CONTROL test asserting that projectBudgetFact, validateUsageMeasurement, MEASUREMENT_FACT_TIER, validateBudgetAccount, validateReserveDeclaration and MAX_BUDGET_METERS are all absent from `Object.keys(scheduler)`, with a hand-written assertion that the checked name list is non-empty. Run and record the red — the namespace assertion must fail naming the seven missing exports, which is also your proof the guard is live.

Publish the seam in packages/scheduler/src/index.ts using the file's existing explicit-named-list style, never `export *`. Add a value export block from ./budget/budget-measurement.js for normalizeUsageMeasurement, MEASUREMENT_ISSUE_CODES, MEASUREMENT_ISSUE_LAYERS and SUPPORTED_SOURCE_PARSER_VERSIONS, and extend the existing ./budget/budget-contract.js block with the values BUDGET_ISSUE_CODES, BUDGET_MEASUREMENT_COVERAGES and BUDGET_MEASUREMENT_SOURCES. Add the type closure: from budget-measurement.js the types LayeredIssue, MeasurementIssueCode, MeasurementIssueLayer, MeasurementResult, NormalizedMeasurement and PricebookBinding; from budget-contract.js the types BudgetIssueCode, BudgetMeasurementCoverage, BudgetMeasurementSource, ObservedIntervalRefs and UsageMeasurementRecord. ObservedIntervalRefs is mandatory, not optional — it is the field type of UsageMeasurementRecord.observedInterval, and publishing the record without it publishes a type no consumer can construct. Do NOT publish projectBudgetFact, PolicyFactInputCompatible, MEASUREMENT_FACT_TIER or validateUsageMeasurement, and do not touch either kernel. Add a short comment in the file's existing voice explaining why the normalizer is published while the bare validator and the policy projection are withheld: the normalizer is the authority that adds the source/coverage matrix, the pricebook binding check and the sequence checks on top of the validator, so publishing the validator alone would let a consumer accept a record the authority refuses. Step 2's namespace and count assertions must now pass.

Prove the published binding is the production authority, driven entirely through the bare package root. In index-surface.test.ts add root-driven semantics tests that import ONLY from "@moe/scheduler" — no deep or relative import into ./budget/ — mirroring the exact code/layer pairs recorded in step 1(c), never re-derived: an accepted UNKNOWN-coverage record with null quantity; the refusal when an UNKNOWN-coverage record carries a non-null quantity; an accepted PARTIAL record whose quantity is a lower bound; a source/coverage combination outside the matrix; a truncated record claiming completion; and a malformed envelope. Each must assert the exact issue code AND the exact refusing layer, and where both a CONTRACT-layer and a MEASUREMENT-layer refusal are reachable, include one of each so the two layers are demonstrably separable rather than assumed. Any swept table must carry a hand-written non-zero cardinality assertion and a `ran` counter checked against it, per the epic's generated-case rail. Prove the TYPE closure separately, because `Object.keys` cannot see types: name all eleven new types in the file's existing `import type { ... } from "@moe/scheduler"` block and annotate real values with them — a `MeasurementResult<NormalizedMeasurement>` holding the normalizer's return, a `UsageMeasurementRecord` literal including its `ObservedIntervalRefs`, and a `LayeredIssue` narrowed on its layer discriminant — so a missing or misnamed type fails typecheck instead of passing invisibly.

VERIFY — the single concentrated gate. (1) Run the exact command `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test` from the repo root in PowerShell and paste the fresh tail with its file/test counts as completion evidence; exit 0 required. (2) PLAIN-NODE BARE-SPECIFIER PROBE, run INLINE and never written to disk (epic rail 5 forbids probe files in commits and they are not owned paths): from inside packages/scheduler, where Node's package self-reference resolves the bare name, run a `node --input-type=module -e` one-liner that imports @moe/scheduler, asserts every one of the seven new runtime bindings is present with its expected typeof/Array.isArray shape, INVOKES normalizeUsageMeasurement on a valid observation and asserts `ok === true`, invokes it on a malformed one and asserts the exact refusing code and layer, and prints a single PASS line with the seven names. A binding that only typechecks but does not load would pass the vitest run and fail here. (3) MUTATION DRILL, the composition proof — record a sha256 of budget-measurement.ts, change ONE issue-code string inside it, and require a ROOT-DRIVEN test from step 4 to redden on that exact code; a green drill means the root test is not reaching the production normalizer. Restore by reverse edit, never `git checkout`, and prove restoration with BOTH the recorded sha256 and `git diff --exit-code -- packages/scheduler/src/budget/budget-measurement.ts`. Run a second drill removing one name from the published list in index.ts and confirm the namespace assertion reddens naming that exact name. (4) Path-attributed repo baseline per the epic rail: run the repo-wide `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` at the merge-base and at HEAD and report the HEAD-minus-merge-base failing-path set intersected with this task's two owned paths; it must be empty, and any foreign red is disclosed verbatim with exact failing lines. (5) Confirm `grep -c ''` still reads 250 for both kernels and that neither appears in `git status --porcelain`.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, then record the consumer edge, then commit. Read the diff as an attacker: can a consumer holding only the published names accept a usage record the production normalizer would refuse? Is any withheld symbol reachable transitively through a published type's structure? Does the published closure let a consumer actually CONSTRUCT a UsageMeasurementRecord, or did an unpublished field type make it read-only in practice? Is every new type genuinely exercised by an annotation rather than merely listed in the import block, where it would be invisible to both `Object.keys` and a careless reader? Did the count bump get hand-written, or derived from the table it is supposed to police? Then satisfy the epic's composition rail — root loadability is explicitly NOT the final composition per task rail 4 — by calling `moe.add_comment` on task-159f4c21ef9149e8a65f24735c9c1475 listing the exact published value and type names, the normalizer's signature including its optional `prior` argument and its deterministic same-identity no-op behaviour, and the fact that projectBudgetFact and validateUsageMeasurement are deliberately withheld so the composer must go through the normalizer. Finally commit by EXPLICIT PATHSPEC naming only packages/scheduler/src/index.ts and packages/scheduler/src/index-surface.test.ts — `git status --porcelain` first, `git restore --staged` anything foreign, then `git show --stat` to confirm neither kernel and no probe or drill leftover landed.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) `export * from "./budget/budget-measurement.js"` — REJECTED. It would drag `projectBudgetFact`, `PolicyFactInputCompatible`, `MEASUREMENT_FACT_TIER` and `validateUsageMeasurement` to the root, which DoD 1 forbids ("no direct enumerator, policy, fixture, or incidental helper leaks"), and index.ts is built entirely from explicit named lists.

2) PUBLISH `validateUsageMeasurement` TOO — REJECTED. The normalizer already composes it and adds the source/coverage matrix, the pricebook binding check and the sequence checks. A consumer holding the bare validator could accept a record the normalizer would refuse, which is precisely the authority bypass this publication exists to prevent.

3) PUBLISH `projectBudgetFact` / `PolicyFactInputCompatible` / `MEASUREMENT_FACT_TIER` — REJECTED as policy. The consumer is a provider TELEMETRY composer; budget-policy projection is a different seam and DoD 1 names policy as a forbidden leak. All three become negative-control assertions instead.

4) OMIT `SUPPORTED_SOURCE_PARSER_VERSIONS` — REJECTED. A composer must set `sourceParserVersion` on every record it builds; without the published vocabulary it must hardcode 1 or 2, which is exactly the "copy the matrix instead of using the authority" failure the objective names. It is a closed vocabulary of the normalizer's own input, not an incidental helper.

5) OMIT `ObservedIntervalRefs` because the DoD's list does not spell it — REJECTED. It is a field type of `UsageMeasurementRecord`; without it the published record type cannot be constructed by a consumer and the publication is decorative. The DoD says "required type closure", and closure is measured from the signature, not from the prose list.

6) APPEND the new names to the end of EXPECTED_EXPORTS — REJECTED; see the ordering trap in codebaseInsights. The comparison sorts only the actual side.
